teams.heading: Lenihan says Fiji 'deserve huge respect' after Farrell makes seven changes
teams.body: Lenihan judged Ireland head coach Andy Farrell's seven changes 'a very balanced selection', but he saved his strongest praise for the visitors. Fiji, he said, 'deserve huge respect' and have 'incredible individual talent', and once they get time to prepare 'they'll be excellent'. He named Josua Tuisova, Juta Wainiqolo, Ben Volavola and Frank Lomani as the backs to watch. Fiji are still without a point in the Southern Hemisphere conference.

lead.why: It is the strongest NEW item in the pack, and it is the only one that gives Fiji their own stake in the story.

teams.heading: Maro Itoje warns England not to sleepwalk into Eddie Jones's Japan test
teams.body: Second-row Maro Itoje has warned England against complacency, saying they cannot "sleepwalk" into Saturday's test at Twickenham. "Japan aren't most teams," Itoje said, so England must stay alive, impose their own game and keep their house in order. Itoje, who made his debut under Eddie Jones in 2016, expects his former coach to throw "weird and wonderful" tactics at them, and Jones has already hinted at unorthodox rugby.

lead.why: It is a fresh England-side story from the Guardian, and Itoje's warning is the pre-match line a fan would pass on, unlike the Ojomoh selection already covered.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus swapped Springboks front row 75 minutes before kick-off against France
teams.body: The South African federation revealed 75 minutes before kick-off that the Springboks' starting and replacement front rows had been exchanged. Rugbyrama reports that Nations Championship rules, unlike those of the World Cup and Six Nations, did not forbid the change, which Rassie Erasmus had already used in the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry. In the build-up, France head coach Fabien Galthié had kept his Marcoussis camp closed to the press, Rugbyrama's Marc Duzan reported. France went on to win 21-19.

lead.why: It is the only new item reporting a concrete event in the France match, and it bears directly on how the Bleus met the Springboks.

teams.heading: Stuart McCloskey says he couldn't care less about Ireland's ageing midfield
teams.body: Ulster centre Stuart McCloskey, 34, was asked this week about the age of Ireland's midfield and was unbothered. He is one of four 30-somethings in a long-running four-way contest with Robbie Henshaw, Garry Ringrose and Bundee Aki. "Honestly, I couldn't care less about the succession of what's going on after me," he told reporters in Abbotstown. The starting XV Andy Farrell picked against Argentina averaged 29.2 years, with eight players aged 30 or over.

teams.heading: Gonzalo Quesada and Azzurri back Genoa shelter's adopt, don't buy campaign
teams.body: Some Azzurri took part in the Captain's Run at Genoa's Stadio Luigi Ferraris on the eve of the Argentina test, then visited the Monte Contessa municipal shelter. Head coach Gonzalo Quesada, municipal councillor Francesca Ghio and shelter volunteers posed with some of the animals as part of the city's adopt, don't buy campaign, which the players helped relaunch. The Federazione Italiana Rugby, working with Genoa city council, presents the visit as part of its social responsibility work.

lead.why: The only fresh Italy item on the shortlist that is not Nicotera's press conference, which is already reported, and Matera's quotes are Argentina's.

teams.heading: Townsend stresses individual responsibility after seven tries conceded to New Zealand
teams.body: The problems against New Zealand were, in Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend's view, more about how the side gave the All Blacks chances inside its 22 than what the defence did. He framed it as individual responsibility, citing a player coming offside or not rolling away quickly. "If you are giving those entries to the best teams in the world, they are looking to score over 50% of the time," Townsend said. Scotland conceded seven tries in the 21-43 defeat in Edinburgh last weekend.

lead.why: Townsend's fresh comments on the New Zealand defeat are a new angle, unlike the already-run team-selection story.

teams.heading: Gregor Paul brands Wales a 'Dickensian orphan' after All Blacks' ten changes
teams.body: The All Blacks have made 10 changes for Saturday's Nations Championship clash in Cardiff, and New Zealand Herald journalist Gregor Paul reads them as a verdict on the hosts. He argues the rotation shows how far Wales have fallen, and that a side once "the lord of the manor" now plays the Dickensian orphan, hoping for a penny. Paul also says Wales sit as the exception among nations whose standards have risen. Wales' last win over New Zealand came in 1953.

lead.why: It is a fresh rival-media verdict on Wales, anchored in the All Blacks' ten changes, and a fan would forward it to a mate.

teams.heading: Pablo Matera replaces injured Montoya as Argentina captain for Italy clash
teams.body: With Montoya sidelined, Argentina captain Pablo Matera has put the set-piece at the centre of Saturday's test against Italy. He said Italy are strong in the static phases, but that Argentina's scrum is very strong, and that with six forwards and two backs on the bench the match will turn on the set-piece. Matera also called the first step after last week's 42-12 loss to Ireland self-criticism, and said the squad trained hard this week.

lead.why: A fresh Argentina item from the captain's press conference on Italy, and it is not already covered by the Contepomi or Quesada editions.

teams.heading: Rob Valetini says Wallabies will lead with actions, not words, against Scotland
teams.body: Wallabies back-rower Rob Valetini returns to the starting side after the England loss, and says the squad has had a hard look at itself. Winger Harry Potter, returning on the left wing after Isaac Henry's hamstring injury sidelined Henry for close to six weeks, says post-match meetings were honest and at times brutal. Valetini wants the Wallabies to lead by actions against Scotland at Murrayfield.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones vows Japan will 'play the house down' against England
teams.body: Japan head coach Eddie Jones, England's boss from 2015 to 2022, has made his bold pledge ahead of Saturday's Twickenham test. England are heavy favourites after their 45-22 win over Australia last week, but Japan arrive having won only one of four matches in this tournament, a 27-10 victory over Italy in Tokyo. They have never beaten England in six attempts.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie says All Blacks will target Wales flanker Jac Morgan
teams.body: New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie says the All Blacks have discussed how to neutralise Wales flanker Jac Morgan, whose contact-area work New Zealand regard as one of Wales' main strengths. Ahead of Saturday's Test at the Principality Stadium, Rennie said we're well aware of that and we'll have a focus on eliminating him before he can cause us stress. Rennie also said the All Blacks must not let Wales scrum-half Tomos Williams have too much space, given his kicking game.

lead.why: It is a fresh, match-specific coach comment on a named Wales threat, and it is not a repeat of the captaincy, bench or maul stories already run.

teams.heading: Calls for World Rugby sanction after Erasmus' late Springbok front-row switch
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus swapped the Springboks' entire starting front row an hour before kick-off in Paris, promoting Jan-Hendrik Wessels, Gerhard Steenekamp and Thomas du Toit. Some pundits and supporters believe the Boks should be punished, and fans want World Rugby to clarify its rules. World Rugby Regulation 15.1.2 requires starting XVs and replacements to be exchanged 48 hours before kick-off, and WalesOnline reports it is unclear whether named replacements may start.

lead.why: A new, South Africa-focused story about whether Rassie Erasmus' late front-row switch against France breaches World Rugby rules.
